title: PID & Tubo-ovarian Abscess
sources: Critical Vector — OB Pocket Guide: PID & TOA (CDC 2021)

changelog.change: Initial entry — minimum diagnostic criteria, hospitalisation indications, inpatient/outpatient regimens, and TOA drainage indications.

summary: Treat empirically at a low threshold: uterine OR adnexal OR cervical motion tenderness in a sexually active patient at risk is enough to start antibiotics — the cost of a missed PID is infertility and chronic pain. All regimens now include metronidazole for anaerobic coverage.

items: Uterine tenderness, OR adnexal tenderness, OR cervical motion tenderness — in a sexually active patient at risk.
Supportive (not required): oral temp > 38.3 °C, mucopurulent cervical discharge, elevated CRP/ESR, WBC > 10k, positive gonorrhoea/chlamydia NAAT.
PID clinical picture PLUS a pelvic mass on exam or imaging (TVUS or CT).
CT is preferred when the diagnosis is uncertain — shows abscess walls, septations, and complexity.
Hospitalise for: TOA, inability to exclude a surgical emergency, pregnancy, severe illness, failure of outpatient therapy, or adherence concerns.

rows: Cefoxitin 2 g IV q6h + doxycycline 100 mg IV/PO q12h
Until clinical improvement ≥ 24–48 h, then doxycycline 100 mg PO BID to complete 14 days total
Clindamycin 900 mg IV q8h + gentamicin 1.5 mg/kg IV q8h (or 5 mg/kg q24h)
Then clindamycin 450 mg PO QID or doxycycline 100 mg PO BID to complete 14 days
Ceftriaxone 500 mg IM ×1 + doxycycline 100 mg PO BID + metronidazole 500 mg PO BID ×14 days
Reassess in 72 h — admit if no improvement

items: CT/US-guided drainage for an abscess ≥ 8 cm, or failure of IV antibiotics after 72 h.
A ruptured abscess is a surgical emergency → theatre.
